items.readable_text:
Content:
When solving a multivariable equation for a particular variable, we sometimes have to factor some terms in the equation to reach the solution.

Content:
For example, let's solve the following equation for the variable [MATH: d\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: 2cd - 3d = 5]

Content:
First, we factor out [MATH: d] in the expression on the left-hand side. This gives

Content:
[MATH: d(2c-3) = 5.]

Content:
Then, we divide both sides of the equation by [MATH: (2c-3)] to isolate [MATH: d\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: d(2c − 3)|= 5; (d(2c − 3))/(2c − 3)|= (5)/(2c − 3); (d(2c − 3))/(2c − 3)|= (5)/(2c − 3); d|= (5)/(2c − 3)]

Content:
Note: This result assumes that [MATH: 2c-3\neq 0.]

[MATH: 2|= wz − 2w + 1; 2 − 1|= wz − 2w + 1 − 1; 1|= wz − 2w]

Next, we factor out [MATH: w] in the expression on the right-hand side.

[MATH: 1|= wz − 2w; 1|= w(z − 2)]

Then, we divide both sides by [MATH: (z-2)] to isolate [MATH: w\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: 1|= w(z − 2); (1)/(z − 2)|= (w(z − 2))/(z − 2); (1)/(z − 2)|= (w(z − 2))/(z − 2); (1)/(z − 2)|= w; w|= (1)/(z − 2)]

Note: This result assumes that [MATH: z-2\neq 0.]

sections.normalized_html:
We need to isolate all terms with [MATH: y] on one side of the equation. To do this, we subtract [MATH: 5y] from both sides:

[MATH: 4ky|= 5y + 1; 4ky − 5y|= 5y + 1 − 5y; 4ky − 5y|= 1]

Notice that all terms containing [MATH: y] are on the left-hand side, and all terms independent of [MATH: y] are on the right-hand side.

Next, we factor out [MATH: y] in the expression on the left-hand side.

[MATH: 4ky − 5y|= 1; y(4k − 5)|= 1]

Finally, we divide both sides by [MATH: (4k -5)] to isolate [MATH: y\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: y(4k − 5)|= 1; (y(4k − 5))/((4k − 5))|= (1)/((4k − 5)); (y(4k − 5))/((4k − 5))|= (1)/(4k − 5); y|= (1)/(4k − 5)]

Note: This result assumes that [MATH: 4k-5\neq 0.]

sections.normalized_html: Solve the equation [MATH: \dfrac{xy}{3} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2}] for the variable [MATH: y.]
sections.readable_text: Solve the equation [MATH: \dfrac{xy}{3} = \dfrac{y - 1}{2}] for the variable [MATH: y.]

sections.normalized_html:
We need to isolate all terms with [MATH: y] on one side of the equation. To do this, we first cross-multiply:

[MATH: (xy)/(3)|= (y − 1)/(2); 2 ⋅ xy|= 3 ⋅ (y − 1); 2xy|= 3y − 3]

Next, we subtract [MATH: 3y] from both sides of the equation:

[MATH: 2xy|= 3y − 3; 2xy − 3y|= 3y − 3 − 3y; 2xy − 3y|= − 3]

Notice that all terms containing [MATH: y] are on the left-hand side, and all terms independent of [MATH: y] are on the right-hand side.

Then, we factor out [MATH: y] from the left-hand side:

[MATH: 2xy − 3y|= − 3; y(2x − 3)|= − 3]

Finally, we divide both sides by [MATH: (2x - 3)] to isolate [MATH: y\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: y(2x − 3)|= − 3; (y(2x − 3))/(2x − 3)|= (− 3)/(2x − 3); (y(2x − 3))/(2x − 3)|= (− 3)/(2x − 3); y|= − (3)/(2x − 3)]

Note: This result assumes that [MATH: 2x-3\neq 0.]

Item 2 — Example: Solving Linear Equations by Factoring

Solve the equation [MATH: 2 = wz - 2w +1] for the variable [MATH: w.]

EXPLANATION

[MATH: 2|= wz − 2w + 1; 2 − 1|= wz − 2w + 1 − 1; 1|= wz − 2w]
